answer: In a data market, agents sell summit maps, nectar surveys, and plume forecasts. Each seller identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before its offers become visible; one deposit cannot back multiple identities. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing financing costs and exposure to token price changes. Cheap account creation no longer buys cheap market presence, though a wealthy attacker can still pay the cost.
